page.question: Is the water under these farms running out, and would the fields show it?

nw_india.label: North-west India
nw_india.statement: Groundwater storage in this region fell by about 4.0 cm of water per year between 2002 and 2026 (range 3.6 to 4.4), about 95 cm in total. In a spell of average rainfall, storage still fell by about 4.1 cm a year (range 2.4 to 5.8), so rainfall alone does not account for the decline. Rainfall itself has been increasing over the period. Over the same years (2002-2025) the region grew greener, by about 0.04 NDVI a decade. Looking at the fields alone, nothing would suggest the water under them was falling. This is an estimate: modelled soil moisture and snow were subtracted from total storage (GLDAS_NOAH025_M v2.1); surface water (lakes, rivers, reservoirs, canals) was not subtracted, because the model has no such store. It does not say why the storage changed. It is a regional average; places inside the region can differ. Greenness leaves out 1 of the region's blocks (4% of its area), which cloud or snow hide in more than a quarter of months. Fields staying green while stored water falls is the pattern a reference study of north-west India links to pumping for irrigation; this check shows the two records side by side and does not test that cause. A change this large is unlikely to be chance: the test used gives a false alarm about 1 time in 20 or less on trend-free records, including ones that wander from year to year. Natural swings much longer than the record cannot be ruled out.
would_strengthen: No independent record has been compared.
An independent record for the same region, such as observation wells.
The uncertainty of the subtracted model carried into the result.

high_plains.label: US High Plains
high_plains.statement: On a straight-line fit, groundwater storage in this region fell by about 1.3 cm of water per year between 2002 and 2026 (range 0.9 to 1.7). Year-to-year changes vary too much for that to pass this project's significance test: a record that simply wanders could look like this. Once rainfall is taken into account, the record points to storage that fell by about 1.5 cm a year (range 0.4 to 2.5) in a spell of average rainfall; that reading is a description, not a tested result. Wetter spells do help: each extra 100 mm of yearly rain goes with about 2.2 cm more storage. Rainfall itself shows no detectable trend over the period. Storage did not show a tested decline, so there is no hidden fall for greenness to mask; greenness showed no clear trend over 2002-2025. This is an estimate: modelled soil moisture and snow were subtracted from total storage (GLDAS_NOAH025_M v2.1); surface water (lakes, rivers, reservoirs, canals) was not subtracted, because the model has no such store. It does not say why the storage changed. It is a regional average; places inside the region can differ. This describes the record. It has not met this project's bar for calling a change statistically significant.
would_strengthen: The calibrated significance test did not fire.
An independent record for the same region, such as observation wells.

playbook.name: water_and_greenness_check
playbook.question: Is the water stored in and under this region changing, does the change follow rainfall, and would the region's greenness show it?

storage_audit.name: storage_audit
storage_audit.description: Check a water-storage record's provenance, what it measures, region size against the provider's resolution, and record length.

storage_annual.name: storage_annual
storage_annual.description: Remove the seasonal cycle with a gap-tolerant harmonic fit and average by calendar year, requiring four months per year and listing the years that rest on fewer than twelve.

storage_trend.name: storage_trend
storage_trend.description: Sen slope with its range, the drift test on year-to-year changes (prewhitened Mann-Kendall is reported as a second method and does not decide), the smallest detectable trend, curvature and period sensitivity for annual storage.

storage_handover.name: storage_handover
storage_handover.description: Rank the change across the declared gap between satellite missions against the same measurement everywhere else in the record, and attach a caution if it stands out.

storage_rainfall.name: storage_rainfall
storage_rainfall.description: Relate yearly change in storage to rainfall accumulated over the same two years; report the change at average rainfall.

storage_greenness.name: storage_greenness
storage_greenness.description: Set the region's yearly greenness beside its yearly water storage over the same years; name whether greenness held, rose or fell while storage changed.
